title: Canonical localization by accumulated energy
source_statement: Let eta be a progressive integrand on a finite horizon [0,T] whose pathwise quadratic energy is finite almost surely. Stop the path when accumulated energy reaches level n+1, using T if that level is never reached. These stopping times form a localizing sequence, and every corresponding stopped integrand is globally square-integrable.
why_it_matters: Theorem 1.1.8 integrates globally L2 processes. Proposition 1.1.13 is the bridge from Chewi's weaker pathwise local-square-integrability assumption to that theory: every energy stop creates a legal global-L2 integrand.
intuition: A_t=integral_0^t eta_s^2 ds is an energy meter. The n-th localizer switches the process off when the meter reaches n+1. Raising the threshold moves the stop later; on a path with finite terminal energy, sufficiently high thresholds are never reached, so the stop eventually equals T.
formula: A_t(omega)=\int_0^t eta_s(omega)^2\,ds,\qquad tau_n(omega)=\inf\{t\le T:A_t(omega)=n+1\}\;\text{ with fallback }T.
source_assumptions: a complete right-continuous filtered probability space
a progressive real integrand eta on [0,T]
pathwise finite quadratic energy on [0,T], almost surely
formal_contracts: SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu, used to obtain the completed adapted energy process needed by the hitting-time proof
IsProbabilityMeasure mu, used only when the pathwise n+1 bound is integrated over omega
LocalProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T, which records progressive measurability and local square integrability without silently strengthening it to global L2

proof_steps.title: 1. Regularize the accumulated energy
proof_steps.text: For each sample omega, the completed energy path A_t is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and continuous, while A_t is measurable using information available at time t. This is the hidden process regularity required by the first-hitting-time argument.

proof_steps.title: 2. Prove the first hit is a stopping time
proof_steps.text: For a nonnegative level c, continuity gives tau_c<=t iff T<=t or A_t>=c. If A_t has crossed c, the intermediate value theorem supplies s<=t with A_s=c. Hence {tau_c<=t} is measurable in F_t. Taking c=n+1 proves each tau_n is a stopping time.

proof_steps.title: 3. Prove monotonicity in the energy level
proof_steps.text: If c<=d, a continuous nondecreasing energy path cannot hit d before it has hit c. Thus higher thresholds give later canonical localizers and tau_n<=tau_{n+1} pathwise.

proof_steps.title: 4. Bound the stopped energy exactly
proof_steps.text: If level n+1 is reached then A_{tau_n}=n+1. If it is not reached, tau_n=T and A_T<n+1; otherwise continuity would create a hit. Therefore the stopped quadratic energy is always at most n+1.

proof_steps.title: 5. Upgrade the stopped process to global L2
proof_steps.text: Stopping preserves progressiveness. Integrating the pathwise bound over the probability measure gives finite expected product-space energy, so eta_s 1_{s<=tau_n} is a ProgressiveL2Integrand and Theorem 1.1.8 applies.

proof_steps.title: 6. Exhaust the finite horizon
proof_steps.text: On a path with finite A_T choose an integer N>A_T. For all sufficiently large n the level n+1 is unreachable, hence tau_n=T. Consequently tau_n tends to T almost surely, completing the localizing-sequence proof.

hidden_details: A first hitting time is not automatically a stopping time: one needs adapted fixed-time energy fields and continuity to identify {tau<=t} with a fixed-time energy event.
The equality-level construction exposes the intermediate-value theorem and prevents an unproved no-overshoot claim.
Pathwise local L2 and expected product-space L2 are different hypotheses; stopping plus the deterministic n+1 bound is what bridges them.
The open/closed endpoint conventions 1_{s<tau} and 1_{s<=tau} agree only in time-integral/L2 sense because a singleton time has zero Lebesgue mass.
Almost-sure finiteness is handled on a full-measure good set; it is not silently converted into a pointwise hypothesis.

title: The local Ito integral is a continuous local martingale
source_statement: For a progressive integrand that is locally square-integrable, its Ito integral, defined by localization, is a continuous local martingale.
why_it_matters: This is where Chewi's local stochastic integral becomes a process with the martingale structure needed by Ito calculus and SDE arguments. Deterministic-horizon existence is insufficient: the localized pieces must agree at random stopping times and glue to one adapted continuous process.
intuition: Proposition 1.1.13 supplies random safety windows on which eta has finite L2 energy. Theorem 1.1.8 gives an ordinary continuous martingale on each window. Proposition 1.1.16 proves that these martingales agree whenever their windows overlap, so they are pieces of one global continuous local martingale rather than unrelated copies.
formula: M_t=\int_0^t eta_s\,dB_s,\qquad M_{t\wedge tau_n}=\int_0^t eta_s\mathbf 1_{\{s\le tau_n\}}\,dB_s.
source_assumptions: a complete right-continuous filtered probability space
Brownian motion relative to that filtration
a progressive integrand with finite quadratic energy on every finite horizon almost surely
formal_contracts: SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu and IsProbabilityMeasure mu
IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu, not merely correct one-time Gaussian marginals
GlobalLocalProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu, recording local square integrability on cofinal finite horizons
the global process version is constructed only after random-stop and cross-horizon consistency are proved

proof_steps.title: 1. Localize eta into the global-L2 theory
proof_steps.text: For every canonical energy localizer on a finite dyadic horizon, eta^k_s=eta_s 1_{s<=tau_k} is progressive and globally L2. Theorem 1.1.8 therefore produces a continuous martingale I^k_t=integral_0^t eta^k_s dB_s.

proof_steps.title: 2. Prove Ito integration commutes with bounded random stopping
proof_steps.text: Start with an elementary process and a grid-valued stopping time, where the identity is exact finite-sum algebra. Approximate a general bounded stopping time from the right by dyadic grid times. Continuous Ito-sum paths identify evaluation at the limiting random time, while product-space L2 convergence of stopped integrands and the Ito isometry transfer the limit through stochastic integration. This yields I(eta 1_{s<=tau})_t=I(eta)_{t wedge tau}, first almost everywhere at fixed times and then on one full-measure set for every time in the horizon.

proof_steps.title: 3. Remove the strict/closed endpoint ambiguity
proof_steps.text: Finite stopping algebra naturally keeps intervals whose left endpoint is strictly before tau, while Chewi uses a closed stopped integrand. The difference lies on the stopping graph {(s,omega):s=tau(omega)}. After proving the graph measurable, singleton time sections have zero Lebesgue mass and Tonelli gives product-measure zero, so both representatives are equal in L2.

proof_steps.title: 4. Prove compatibility across deterministic horizons
proof_steps.text: The construction uses horizons 1,2,4,... . Extending a smaller stopped integrand by zero to a larger horizon gives exactly the same L2 element as stopping the larger-horizon integrand at the smaller localizer. Ito congruence then identifies the stochastic integrals on the overlap.

proof_steps.title: 5. Make the localized martingales coherent
proof_steps.text: For k<=ell, the ell-th martingale stopped at the k-th canonical localizer agrees pathwise almost surely with the k-th martingale over the earlier horizon. A countable intersection gives one full-measure event on which all overlap identities hold simultaneously.

proof_steps.title: 6. Glue one adapted continuous global version
proof_steps.text: On the common good set define M_t using any sufficiently large localized horizon; overlap consistency makes the choice irrelevant. Use a harmless default on the null exceptional set. This proves strong adaptedness and continuity of a single chosen process rather than confusing L2 equivalence classes with pointwise paths.

proof_steps.title: 7. Verify the local-martingale definition
proof_steps.text: The global canonical localizers increase to infinity almost surely. Stopping M at the k-th localizer recovers the k-th globally square-integrable Ito martingale. Hence M is a local martingale, and the gluing step already supplied path continuity.

hidden_details: A deterministic-time identity is not enough for a process-level local-martingale theorem; one needs compatible identities on a common full-measure event across the times used for gluing.
A random stopping time cannot be substituted into a deterministic-time theorem without first proving a stopping theorem for the stochastic integral.
Strict and closed stopped-integrand conventions differ on the stopping graph; product-measure nullity, not informal endpoint intuition, makes them the same L2 element.
L2 limits are equivalence classes, while the theorem asserts a continuous process; choosing continuous versions and proving indistinguishability is a separate layer.
Finite-horizon constructions do not automatically define one global process; zero extension, cross-horizon overlap, and countable gluing are required.
Brownian motion must be Brownian relative to the filtration so the martingale/isometry arguments have the required conditional independence.
